Verified directly against the pinned corpus (`/root/.xerj-code/corpora/lmdb/lmdb`, commit `700e10f91a65`, found via `xerj code lmdb "MDB_MAXKEYSIZE default compile-time value" --url http://localhost:9200`):

- **Default value: 0.** `mdb.c:712-714` — `#ifndef MDB_MAXKEYSIZE` → `#define MDB_MAXKEYSIZE 0`. (The doc comment just above notes 511 was the LMDB 0.9 default; 0 is the modern default.)
- **Runtime behavior when 0:** the max key size is computed per-environment from the page size at env-open time, instead of using a compile-time constant. The accessor macro is **`ENV_MAXKEY(env)`** (`mdb.c:716-721`): `#if MDB_MAXKEYSIZE` → `(MDB_MAXKEYSIZE)`, `#else` → `((env)->me_maxkey)`. The field is **`MDB_env.me_maxkey`** (`unsigned int`, `mdb.c:1714-1715`, only present under `#if !(MDB_MAXKEYSIZE)`), set in the env-open path at `mdb.c:5658-5660`: `env->me_maxkey = env->me_nodemax - (NODESIZE + sizeof(MDB_db))`, where `me_nodemax` derives from `me_pagespace` (page size minus page header). `mdb_env_get_maxkeysize()` exposes this to callers.

ANSWER: MDB_MAXKEYSIZE defaults to 0 (mdb.c:712-714); when 0, the code computes the real limit at runtime from the env's page size into the `MDB_env.me_maxkey` field and reads it through the `ENV_MAXKEY(env)` macro (set at mdb.c:5659 as `me_nodemax - (NODESIZE + sizeof(MDB_db))`); a nonzero compile-time value instead makes `ENV_MAXKEY(env)` return the constant directly.
